intent.raw: get all definitions and node types, and prepare a candidate for a canonical definition of 'What is an ontology' and propose a node schema, inside projects/ontologize/. use definitions-governance to create the candidate definitions.
intent.objective: Gather every existing ontologize definition and node type from the project artifacts, then under definitions-governance author a candidate project-canonical definition of 'ontology' (plus the supporting canonical terms ontology node, ontology branch, governed edge) and propose a machine-checkable ontology node schema, without promoting any term to canonical Arcanum or CyberAlchemy vocabulary and keeping GoldenQuill source read-only.
intent.operator_sentence: Read the existing ontologize definitions and the six node types first, then write a candidate canonical definition of 'ontology' and a node schema that encodes the project's own honesty gates.

technique_overlays.trigger: The route produces a definition of 'ontology' and a node schema that could be mistaken for promoted canonical vocabulary or a shipped contract.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every new definition is marked candidate/seed/source-backed with a contradiction path; the node schema is labelled candidate; neither promotes Arcanum/CyberAlchemy vocabulary nor commits client-facing terms.

steps.name: Gather all existing definitions and the six node types from project artifacts
stop_conditions: Block if the six node types (N1-N6) or the four branches (B1-B4) cannot be located in the source artifacts.
Flag and record missing-source residue if a referenced artifact is absent.

steps.name: Author candidate canonical definition of 'ontology' plus supporting terms

capability_metadata.note: definitions-governance is an installed Arcanum skill but is not in the validator's narrow canonical set; treated as a candidate capability here.

convergence_criteria: A canonical definition of 'ontology' (DEF-ONT-001) states a one-line, a plain-language intuition, a normative structural definition, an operational interpretation, neighbor boundaries, and a contradiction path.
Supporting terms (ontology node, ontology branch, governed edge) are defined with stable IDs and status tags.
The index is synchronized and a drift audit reconciles against GLOSSARY.md, the layered DEFINITIONS.md, ONTOLOGY-BRANCHES.md, and DAG-AND-METRICS.md.
stop_conditions: Block canonical promotion of any term to Arcanum or CyberAlchemy vocabulary.
Flag any definition lacking a status tag or contradiction path.

steps.name: Propose a candidate machine-checkable ontology node schema

capability_metadata.note: ontology-vault is an installed Arcanum skill but is not in the validator's narrow canonical set; treated as a candidate capability here.

convergence_criteria: The schema covers all six node types (N1-N6) with a discriminator on node_type.

Per-type honesty gates are encoded: source on OutcomeEvent; veracidade + evidence_refs on N3/N4/N6; denominator on MetricObservation; contradiction_path on PromotionCandidate; record_kind=promotion_record on KnowledgeProjection; veracidade=high requires non-empty evidence_refs.
Edges reference the governed edge catalog edge_type set; an example node validates against the schema.
stop_conditions: Block if the schema drops a node type or a deterministic honesty gate.
Flag if the example node does not validate.

steps.name: Validate dispatch and record open residue plus next route
convergence_criteria: The dispatch validates against the dispatch-spec validator.
Open residue (e.g. primary-branch mapping, undefined-but-load-bearing terms) has named next objects and owners.
stop_conditions: Flag if open residue lacks an owner or next route.

validation: Six node types (N1-N6) located in DAG-AND-METRICS.md §2; four branches (B1-B4) in ONTOLOGY-BRANCHES.md; layered and client-facing definitions read.

DEF-ONT-001 'ontology' carries one-line, intuition, structural definition, operational interpretation, boundaries, contradiction path; DEF-ONT-002/003/004 added with IDs and status tags; index synced; drift audit reconciles downstream surfaces.
Schema covers N1-N6 with node_type discriminator and per-type honesty gates; example MetricObservation node validates.
Dispatch validates against scripts/validate-dispatch.py; open residue recorded in the drift audit with owners.

boundaries.contract: Canonical definitions and the node schema are written only under projects/ontologize as candidate artifacts; they are not promoted to canonical Arcanum or CyberAlchemy vocabulary without owner review.

state_namespaces.write_policy: Definitions and schema artifacts may be written under projects/ontologize only unless a later approved task expands scope.
Read-only source evidence; no GoldenQuill writes.
No writes from this dispatch without an explicit owner-review task.

promotion_splits.source: projects/ontologize candidate canonical definitions and node schema
promotion_splits.target: canonical Arcanum vocabulary or client-facing CyberAlchemy collateral
promotion_splits.rule: requires owner review and a separate promotion route

gates.condition: Every node type, branch, and field in the definitions and schema must trace to an existing ontologize artifact or be explicitly marked as a candidate adaptation.
Each canonical term must carry a status (candidate, seed, or source-backed) and the canonical 'ontology' definition must carry a contradiction path.
A drift audit must reconcile the new canonical definitions against GLOSSARY.md, the layered DEFINITIONS.md, ONTOLOGY-BRANCHES.md, and DAG-AND-METRICS.md.
The node schema must cover all six node types and encode the deterministic honesty gates; an example node must validate.
Outputs may propose candidate canonical definitions and a candidate node schema but must not promote glossary, ontology, sigil, spell, memory, or runtime authority, nor commit client-facing terms.
The dispatch must pass the dispatch-spec validator before being treated as handoff-ready.

promotion_guardrails: Do not modify the GoldenQuill project; treat it as read-only source evidence.
Do not promote ontologize canonical definitions into canonical Arcanum vocabulary without owner review.
Do not treat the candidate node schema as a shipped contract.
Do not commit client-facing terms without owner review.
